floor: PE-Xa or PE-RT pipes at 150–200 mm
Lets the screed expand without cracks
XPS or EPS under the heating
fplate: Concrete grade per design, two rebar meshes
Keeps cement paste out of the insulation
Extruded polystyrene: takes no water, keeps heat in
Torch-on, lapped and turned up the edges
A firm level base for the waterproofing
Keeps the bed from mixing with soil
fstrip: Protects the insulation and sheds water
Cage of longitudinal and transverse bars
net: Cables from the panel: lighting, sockets, dedicated appliance circuits
Cold and hot water from the main to every point
Heat-recovery unit: fresh air to rooms, extract from kitchen and bathrooms
roof: Spacing to the profile; solid deck for standing seam
A vent gap that takes moisture and heat away
Keeps water out, lets vapour out
Insulation between rafters with no gaps
Taped joints keep indoor moisture out of the wool
roof_flat: Turned up the parapet, heated outlets
roof_ter: Inverted roof: insulation above the membrane
slab: Hollow-core or cast — per structural design
slab_c: Keeps the heat in the house
ushp: A thin reinforced slab with pipes cast in
Two staggered layers, L-blocks at the edges
A perimeter pipe takes water away from the slab
w_block: Adhesive with glass mesh — no cracks
Mineral wool is vapour-open and non-combustible
w_brick: Takes moisture out of the insulation
Boards on anchors, wall ties through them
w_frame: Timber boards, fibre cement or render
Battens and wool, cables run here
win: Keeps rain out, lets moisture escape
Keeps indoor vapour out of the joint

b_w1: Aerated block on thin-bed adhesive (2–3 mm joints), the first course on mortar over the damp-proof layer. Every 4th course is reinforced, lintels over openings.
b_w2: First floor, ring beam, wall plate
First-floor walls the same way, topped with a second ring beam with cast-in studs that hold the timber wall plate.
base: Geotextile on the bottom, then sand and crushed stone in compacted layers. The geotextile keeps the bed from mixing with the soil.
belt1: Formwork, a rebar cage and concrete around the perimeter: the ring beam spreads the floor load and ties the walls together.
done: We inspect the house with you, sign the acts, hand over the as-built documents and the keys. Warranty: 12 months.
f_fin: Battens over the vapour barrier leave room for cables and pipes, so the barrier stays intact. Then plasterboard and filler.
f_ins: Mineral wool between studs with no gaps, a breathable wind membrane outside and a taped vapour barrier inside.
f_osb: OSB/3 sheathing outside gives the frame its stiffness. Floor joists on hangers carry the first-floor deck.
f_plate: Treated timber on a damp-proof layer, anchored to the slab — the base for the whole frame.
f_studs: Studs of kiln-dried planed timber spaced to the insulation width, doubled at openings, with headers and a top plate.
f_w2: Studs, plates and OSB on the first floor the same way; the top plate acts as the wall plate.
fac_b: Mineral wool or EPS on adhesive and anchors, a mesh-reinforced base coat, primer and decorative render.
fac_f: Counter-battens create a ventilated gap for the cladding: timber boards, fibre-cement panels or a render system — per the design.
fac_k: Mineral wool on the wall, a ventilated cavity and facing brick on wall ties — a weatherproof facade with no render.
geo: Our surveyor maps the terrain, sets out the house axes on the ground and builds batter boards that every later measurement starts from.
hydro: Waterproofing and XPS under the slab
A concrete blinding layer, torch-on waterproofing with overlaps and XPS boards: the slab stays dry and keeps heat out of the ground.
int: Finishes from the design project, a kitchen and wardrobes by our joiners, light fittings — and the lights come on.
k_belt: A cast ring beam or reinforced bed joint under the planks — per the structural design: a level bearing and a tie between walls.
k_w1: Bonded brickwork on cement-sand mortar, bed-joint mesh every 4–5 courses, lintels over openings.
k_w2: First-floor brickwork, a beam under the roof, the wall plate on studs over a damp-proof layer; wall ties are left for the facing brick.
land: A perimeter path with drainage, walkways, lawn, trees and outdoor lighting — per the landscape design.
mep: Wiring from a panel with breakers and RCDs, water and sloped drainage, boiler and underfloor heating, balanced ventilation — per the MEP design.
pit: We strip the topsoil and dig the pit for the slab to the design depth; the spoil is stockpiled, part of it goes back as backfill.
pour: A concrete pump places the mix, a poker vibrator compacts it; then curing: we keep it damp and covered while it gains strength.
r_crown: Over the footing waterproofing go a sole board and the first course of treated beam, fixed to the footing with studs.
r_fin: We sand the walls and apply antiseptic, fire protection and a stain or oil — the wood breathes and keeps its colour.
r_rafters: Rafters sit on sliding brackets on the top course, so the roof does not pull the walls as they settle; then membrane and counter-battens.
r_shrink: A beam house settles: screw jacks under the posts are adjusted and joints are caulked. Finishes go in after settling.
r_slab: Beams are notched into the courses with an allowance for settling, carrying the first-floor deck.
r_w2: First-floor walls the same way; the top course carries the rafters.
r_walls: Courses go on jute or flax sealing strips and are pinned with dowels; corners get a tight interlocking joint.
r_win: Windows and doors go into floating sub-frames with a settling gap; the joint is sealed with tapes.
rafters: Rafters on the wall plate, then a vapour-open roofing membrane, counter-battens for ventilation and battens for the roofing.
rebar: Two rebar meshes on chairs (concrete cover), edge cages and starter bars for cast-in-place parts. The site manager signs off the rebar before the pour.
roof: Metal tiles or standing seam on battens, gutters; mineral wool between rafters, a vapour barrier below. Mykhailo films the roof by drone.
s_hydro: Bitumen coating, XPS on the plinth, a dimpled drainage membrane — then compacted backfill.
s_pour: We pour the footing with vibration and no cold joints, then cover it and keep it damp while it cures.
s_rebar: We set the formwork and tie a 3D cage of longitudinal and transverse bars, leaving starter bars for the walls.
screed: Screed over the heating pipes with an edge strip, walls plastered to guide beads — a true base for the finishes.
slab: Hollow-core planks by crane or a cast-in-place slab with two meshes — per the structural design. Mykhailo films the progress by drone.
trench: We dig the strip-footing trenches along the axes from the batter boards; width and depth follow the structural design and frost depth.
ushp: XPS on the bed and L-blocks at the edges; underfloor heating pipes and service entries go in before the concrete, with mesh on top.
win: Energy-efficient windows on anchors with a three-layer joint: a breathable tape outside, foam in the gap, a vapour-tight tape inside.

f_ins: Mineral wool between the frames without gaps and a vapour barrier inside: the A-frame slopes act as walls and roof.
f_osb: OSB on frames and a mezzanine
OSB-3 on the frames adds stiffness; mezzanine joists sit on the frames with full-height space below.
f_studs: Triangular frames of dry planed or glulam timber at 1–1.2 m centres: they are walls and roof at once.
f_w2: Studs and rails for big gable windows; the rear gable is more solid and insulated.
fac_f: Around the glass: counter battens and cladding, boards or fibre cement on a vented gap.
rafters: A breathable membrane over the OSB, counter battens for a vented gap from eaves to ridge, then roof battens.
roof: Standing seam or shingles on battens; mineral wool between frames with a taped vapour barrier inside.
win: Gable glazing with a warm installation: tapes outside and inside, foam in the joint; the door in the centre.

b_w2: Attic knee walls and wall plate
Knee walls of about 1 m in aerated block, a ring beam with studs and the wall plate on top. The roof is steeper: an attic needs headroom.
f_w2: Knee wall studs on the floor deck, a top plate for the rafters; the attic is insulated along the rafters.
k_w2: Attic knee walls and wall plate
Knee walls of about 1 m, a ring beam under the roof and the wall plate on studs over damp-proofing.
r_w2: A few knee-wall courses and a top course for the rafters, with room for settling.
roof: Mineral wool between rafters, a vapour barrier below: the attic is a living floor. Roof windows sit in the roof plane with flashing kits.

fac_b: Mineral wool on anchors, a wind membrane, counter battens for a vented gap and cladding: boards, slats or fibre cement to suit the style.
fac_k: Mineral wool on anchors, a wind membrane, counter battens (vented gap) and cladding: boards, slats or fibre cement to suit the style.

rafters: A roof slab per the structural design, a parapet all round and falls to the roof outlets so water never sits on the roof.
roof: Vapour barrier, insulation, a PVC membrane turned up the parapet, a drip edge and heated outlets.

b_w2: A flat roof: starter bars for a cast parapet and roof fixings go into the ring beam and slab. No wall plate is needed.
f_w2: Framing for a flat roof: a double top plate and roof joists with solid decking for the falls.
k_w2: A flat roof: a cast ring beam on the slab with starter bars for the parapet; no wall plate, flexible ties for the facing brick.

b_w2: Upper-floor walls in the same method topped with a ring beam for the roof slab: a flat roof needs no wall plate.
f_w2: Studs, plates and OSB for the upper floor; the top plate carries the flat-roof joists.
k_w2: Upper-floor brickwork and a cast ring beam for the roof slab; flexible ties left for the facing brick.

rafters: Four slopes: hip rafters, jack rafters and shorter rafters at the hips, then membrane, counter battens and battens.
roof: Tiles on battens, gutters all round; mineral wool between the rafters with a vapour barrier below. Mykhailo films the roof by drone.

b_w2: A single-storey house: studs, damp-proofing and the wall plate go on the ring beam and slab to carry the rafters.
f_w2: A single-storey frame: double top plate and ceiling joists spaced for insulation; the rafters sit on them.
k_w2: A ring beam under the roof on the slab, the wall plate on studs over damp-proofing; flexible ties left for the facing brick.
r_w2: The top log course up to design height carries the rafters; ceiling beams are notched in with room for settling.
roof: Roofing on battens and gutters all round; the loft stays cold and ventilated, with insulation laid on the ceiling slab.
slab: A slab or ceiling joists per the structural design, topped with loft insulation or forming the base of a flat roof. Mykhailo films progress by drone.

fac_f: Membrane, render boards on the frame, a mesh-reinforced base coat and decorative render: a timber frame finished in render.

roof: An inverted build-up: membrane, XPS and geotextile, tiles on adjustable pedestals; glass railing and a roof access.
